newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures down on long lquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures down on long lquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on continued long liquidation in active trading on Thursday, traders said.
The key March 1997 contract ended at 3,122 yuan ($376) per tonne, rising 14 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,130 and hit a low of 3,120.
May fell 78 to 3,039, July one to 3,250, September 13 to 3,337, and November four to 3,351.
Traders said many investors were still eager to liquidate long positions in the last two trading days before the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
"Selling pressure was heavy because of the holiday mood," one trader said. "Volume rose sharply, indicating mixed sentiment toward future market trends after the sharp falls of the past few days."
Traders said soybeans were likely to find support at low levels on Friday.
